prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1457; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The insured reported a rear-end collision at a low-speed intersection and the claimant's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped. The claimant reports neck pain and was not represented by an attorney at first contact.

Entry 2: Photos taken at the scene show damage to the rear bumper and trunk area of the claimant's vehicle, which lines up with the impact described. The driver is named on the policy and the coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Our contact with the claimant covered the same account of events as the first call, with no changes to the sequence or the location. There are no independent witnesses, so the photos and the statements are the main sources we have.

Entry 4: The reported neck injury fits the kind and force of a rear impact of this type. No earlier injury to the same body area is known, and nothing in the file suggests prior damage to the vehicle or damage that predates the policy start.

Entry 5: The claimant's treatment followed a usual course and eased off as recovery progressed. Records are still being gathered, and it is not fully clear from the file where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting at impact.

Entry 6: Vehicle damage was reviewed against the reported impact and matches the described collision. Based on what is in the file, the claim is moving forward for further evaluation of the injury portion.
